spec_match.rationale: Fixed 2026-10-25: the dead (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) branch — an unknown query inside @container that parses but can never match — is replaced by a real `tile style(--compact: on)` branch the user can fire, and the prose now teaches explicitly that media conditions are tolerated-but-never-matching inside @container (the behaviour the suite's fallback-with-unknown-feature assertion proves). Verified on Chromium 153: 360/540/720 match on size, all five match with the compact flag.

interactive.rationale: The compact-flag toggle fires the style() branch across all frames, the conditionText button makes a real CSSOM call, show/hide filters the matrix, and the engine-verdict line reports each frame's computed ::before verdict — all driven headless.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card and lede now both describe a container-size branch plus a style() custom-property branch, matching the implementation (the wrong user-preference framing is gone from both).

edge_cases.rationale: The no-match verdict is now the unconditioned default, so a parser that drops the comma rule shows an honest 'no match' everywhere instead of blank verdicts, and a CSSOM capability probe surfaces a requires-Chrome-150 notice when the rule is absent (hidden on this supporting build, verified).

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6196591858941952 and the CSS Conditional 5 container-rule section.

conformance.rationale: Four of five assertions pass on fully-supporting Chromium 153 and genuinely pin the contract; the fifth, comma-list-parses-via-supports, fails even here because CSS.supports parses @supports grammar and never accepts a top-level comma list — flagged for a human below, not edited (assertions are immutable).

runtime_evidence.rationale: chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session, so per auto-research.md §0 this is NOT MCP browser verification — but every control was driven via headless Chromium 153 (Playwright/CDP over the real Chrome binary): compact toggle on/off, show/hide filters, conditionText readback, per-frame computed ::before verdicts; zero console errors and failed requests; screenshots read at 1280×800 and 360×740 DPR3; re-run fresh after the final edit.

telemetry_health.rationale: The page asserts `breakpoint-matrix-verdicts-match-spec` (computed verdicts vs the spec expectation given parse support and flag state) on load and every toggle.

design_system.rationale: Colours from variables (including the color-mix of --accent-emerald); .ctl.on overrides background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: All three toggles expose aria-pressed, the engine-verdict line is a polite text live region mirroring the ::before pseudo-content verdicts, and #cssom-out is aria-live so the conditionText readback is announced.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×740 DPR3 touch and 1280×800: the 540/720px frame bodies scroll inside their own cards (overflow-x) instead of bleeding, no horizontal page overflow on either class, and every control was driven on both.

openQuestions.title: FLAG FOR HUMAN: conformance assertion comma-list-parses-via-supports cannot pass on any browser
openQuestions.detail: The assertion tests CSS.supports('(min-width: 300px), (min-height: 300px)'), but CSS.supports parses a <supports-condition> (@supports grammar), which has never accepted a top-level comma list — it returns false on Chromium 153 even though the other four assertions prove full comma-separated @container support. The assertion cannot detect this feature and will read as a permanent failure on every build. Conformance suites are immutable, so this needs a human to retire or replace it (e.g. with the CSSContainerRule parse probe the suite already has).

summary: Repaired 2026-10-25 (weekly hardening): the dead prefers-reduced-motion branch is replaced by a user-firable style(--compact: on) branch with a toggle, and the prose now teaches that media conditions inside @container are tolerated-but-never-matching unknown queries; the frames use content-box sizing so the labelled 360px trigger genuinely measures 360px and matches (it previously measured ≈334px and never fired); the no-match verdict is the unconditioned default so pre-150 parsers show honest text instead of blanks, with a CSSOM capability notice; frames scroll within their cards; toggles expose aria-pressed and verdicts/conditionText are live regions with a telemetry assert. Verified on headless Chromium 153 (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): flag-off verdicts no/no/match/match/match, flag-on all match, conditionText 'tile (min-width: 360px), tile style(--compact: on)', clean console/network on desktop and mobile, fresh reload after the final edit. One immutable conformance assertion is flagged for a human (see openQuestions).
